thread:
Maria Gomez: FYI team — scheduling a planned maintenance window for the control-plane DB migration on Wed 2026-03-25 02:00-04:00 UTC. This is an unavoidable schema migration to remove legacy tokens. Expected customer-visible impact: up to ~10-15m of control-plane read-only behavior during cutover where new token issuance and some management API calls will return 503. Inference runtime should continue to serve existing sessions. Posting the ops playbook + customer/status page drafts below. Please review asap. @Kevin Ho you will be primary oncall; @Tara Singh backup.

Kevin Ho: ack. Can you add the exact statuspage copy and a short customer template? Also, how are we confirming inference continuity (smoke checks)?

Maria Gomez: draft status page update (T-24h -> T+complete):

- At maintenance_start:
  "We will be performing a scheduled maintenance to migrate the control-plane database. During the migration, management APIs (token issuance, project config updates) may be temporarily unavailable for ~10-15 minutes. Inference serving will continue but some control-plane features may be degraded. We expect full restoration within the maintenance window. Updates will follow here and to affected customers."

- At maintenance_complete:
  "Maintenance complete. All control-plane services are restored. Please contact support if you see any lingering issues."

Customer-facing email template (short):

Subject: Planned maintenance on 2026-03-25 — brief control-plane interruption

Hello,

We're performing a scheduled maintenance to upgrade our control-plane database on Wednesday, 2026-03-25 from 02:00–04:00 UTC. During a brief portion of the window (estimated 10–15 minutes) some management APIs (token issuance, project updates) may be unavailable. Inference requests for active sessions are expected to continue. We'll send updates on progress and confirm when maintenance completes.

If this maintenance would cause an unacceptable impact, please reply and we'll work to schedule an alternative.

Thanks,
The Redwood Inference Ops Team

Kevin Ho: LGTM. Add the following ops checklist to the thread so oncall has a clear playbook. Also I'm going to schedule the statuspage entries at T-60m and T+0 automatically.

Maria Gomez: Ops checklist (in order):
1) T-24h: Notify customers (email + status page scheduled).
2) T-2h: Run pre-flight (see commands).
3) T-30m: Prepare rollback snapshot and confirm backups are healthy.
4) T-10m: Set maintenance mode in control plane (routing still active).
5) T+0: Start schema migration. Expect 10–15m where token issuance returns 503.
6) T+15m: Run post-migration sanity checks.
7) T+30m: Monitor metrics; handback to normal ops.

Pre-flight commands (run from infra-ops workstation):
```
# check control-plane health
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=control-plane
# verify backup snapshot
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-backups/control-plane/ --recursive | tail -n 5
# test token issuance on staging
curl -X POST https://control-plane.staging.redwood.ai/tokens -d '{"project":"smoke"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

Sim Patel: Quick question — you said inference should continue. Are there any edge cases where running jobs might reconnect to control-plane for auth? We should warn customers who rely on short-lived tokens.

Maria Gomez: Good call. Add this line to customer email: "If your integration relies on creating new short-lived tokens during requests, expect potential failures during the cutover window. Consider provisioning tokens ahead of time." I'll add an FAQ note on the status page.

Tara Singh: On-call handoff plan:
- Primary: Kevin Ho (pager: +1-555-0102 slack: @kevin)
- Backup: Tara Singh (pager: +1-555-0203 slack: @tara)
- Escalation: Sim Patel -> Jordan Lee -> Eng Director (if not acked in 15m)

Contact routing: use #eng-oncall for initial triage, escalate to #eng-platform for infra-level rollback. For customer comms, include support-bot to create a ticket and tag affected customers.

Jordan Lee: I'll pre-generate the rollback runbook and snapshot restore steps. Quick snippet for rollback toggle: 
```
# feature flag toggle to bypass new auth flow
curl -X POST https://control-plane.redwood.ai/flag -d '{"name":"auth_migration","state":"off"}'
```

incident-bot: Scheduled Maintenance created by Maria Gomez: maintenance_id=mc-2145938271, window=2026-03-25T02:00:00Z/2026-03-25T04:00:00Z, visibility=public. Notifications scheduled at T-24h, T-60m, T-0.

support-bot: Support ticket templates created: #TKT-9871 (Low impact) and #TKT-9872 (Customers with short-lived tokens). Assigned to Support Ops queue.

Kevin Ho: A couple of runbook clarifications:
- Monitoring to watch: control-plane 5xx rate, token issuance latency, auth-failed counts from gateway logs, consumer backpressure on router.
- SLO impact estimate: negligible for inference throughput, possible small window of elevated 503 for management APIs.

Tara Singh: Any special customers to ping directly? We have the list from account-exec: 3 customers running token-on-every-request. Jordan can you add them to #customer-pings?

Jordan Lee: Done — I added the three to the manual ping list and drafted bespoke notes.

Maria Gomez: final checklist additions:
- Confirm oncall phone numbers are reachable at T-15m.
- Post start to #statuspage and #eng-oncall with exact start time.
- If rollback needed, follow Jordan's restore steps and post to status page with estimated ETA.

Kevin Ho: I'll be standing by. Please escalate immediately if we see >5% 5xx or token issuance fails beyond 20 minutes.

Maria Gomez: Thanks everyone. I'll push the scheduled statuspage posts now and send the customer email at T-24h. If you have edits to the templates, drop them here and I'll update. :white_check_mark:

Tara Singh: one last note — adding a quick post-mortem template to the thread so we don't forget to capture timing and impact after maintenance:
- Start time:
- End time:
- Actual customer impact (list customers)
- Root cause summary
- Next steps / follow-ups

Maria Gomez: perfect. Closing out for now — will reopen thread if any new info.
